# Summary of Python Files in `agents/`

The `agents/` directory contains a progressive tutorial series (s01 → s12) showing how to build a Claude-style coding agent, plus a capstone `s_full.py` that combines every mechanism. Each file is **self-contained, runnable** (`python agents/sXX_*.py`), and uses the Anthropic SDK with a REPL prompt. All scripts share a small set of base tools (`bash`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) implemented with a workspace-sandboxed `safe_path()` helper.

Common dependencies across all files: `anthropic`, `python-dotenv`, plus stdlib `os`, `subprocess`, `pathlib`. Environment requires `MODEL_ID` (and optional `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`).

---

## `agents/__init__.py`
- **Purpose:** Package marker / brief manifesto.
- **Content:** A 3-line comment stating "The model is the agent. These files are the harness." Files s01–s12 are progressive harness implementations; `s_full` is the reference.

---

## `agents/s01_agent_loop.py` — The Agent Loop
- **Purpose:** Distills the *entire* secret of a coding agent into one pattern: `while stop_reason == "tool_use": call LLM → run tools → append results`.
- **Key components:**
  - `run_bash(command)` — sandboxed shell with dangerous-command blocklist and 120s timeout.
  - `agent_loop(messages)` — the canonical loop; one tool (`bash`) is exposed.
  - Optional `readline` setup for macOS libedit UTF-8 fix.
- **Notable:** Demonstrates the core idea that everything later is just policy layered on this loop.

---

## `agents/s02_tool_use.py` — Tools
- **Purpose:** Shows that adding tools doesn't change the loop — only the dispatch map grows.
- **Key components:**
  - Adds `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file` alongside `bash`.
  - `TOOL_HANDLERS` dict — name→lambda dispatch table.
  - `safe_path()` — prevents path escapes from workspace.
- **Notable insight:** "The loop didn't change. I just added tools."

---

## `agents/s03_todo_write.py` — TodoWrite (Planning)
- **Purpose:** Gives the model a structured way to plan and track multi-step work.
- **Key components:**
  - `TodoManager` class — validates ≤20 items, only one `in_progress` at a time, statuses (`pending`/`in_progress`/`completed`).
  - `TODO.render()` — pretty-printed checklist with `[ ]`, `[>]`, `[x]`.
  - **Nag reminder mechanism:** if the model goes ≥3 rounds without using the `todo` tool, the harness injects `<reminder>Update your todos.</reminder>` into the next user turn.
- **Notable insight:** "The agent can track its own progress — and I can see it."

---

## `agents/s04_subagent.py` — Subagents (Context Isolation)
- **Purpose:** Spawn a child agent with `messages=[]` for isolated exploration; only its final summary returns to the parent.
- **Key components:**
  - `run_subagent(prompt)` — fresh context, capped at 30 iterations, child cannot recursively spawn (`CHILD_TOOLS` omits `task`).
  - `SUBAGENT_SYSTEM` — separate system prompt.
  - Parent has all base tools + a `task` tool that dispatches subagents.
- **Notable insight:** "Process isolation gives context isolation for free."

---

## `agents/s05_skill_loading.py` — Skills (On-Demand Knowledge)
- **Purpose:** Two-layer skill injection so the system prompt isn't bloated.
- **Key components:**
  - `SkillLoader` — scans `skills/**/SKILL.md`, parses YAML frontmatter (name, description, tags).
  - **Layer 1:** Short skill names + descriptions injected into system prompt (~100 tokens each).
  - **Layer 2:** Full skill body returned via `load_skill(name)` tool only when needed.
- **Notable dependency:** `yaml` (PyYAML) for frontmatter parsing.
- **Notable insight:** "Don't put everything in the system prompt. Load on demand."

---

## `agents/s06_context_compact.py` — Compact (Memory Compression)
- **Purpose:** Three-tier compression pipeline so an agent can run indefinitely.
- **Key components:**
  - **Layer 1 — `micro_compact()`:** Each turn, replaces non-`read_file` tool_results older than the last 3 with `[Previous: used <tool>]`.
  - **Layer 2 — `auto_compact()`:** When token estimate > 50K, saves full transcript to `.transcripts/transcript_<ts>.jsonl`, asks the LLM to summarize, then replaces the entire history with that summary.
  - **Layer 3 — `compact` tool:** Model can manually trigger summarization (with optional `focus`).
  - `estimate_tokens()` — rough `len(str)/4` heuristic.
- **Notable insight:** "The agent can forget strategically and keep working forever."

---

## `agents/s07_task_system.py` — Tasks (Persistent Goals)
- **Purpose:** Tasks survive context compression because they live as files outside the conversation.
- **Key components:**
  - `TaskManager` — CRUD over `.tasks/task_<id>.json`, auto-increments IDs, supports a `blockedBy` dependency graph.
  - `_clear_dependency()` — completing a task automatically removes it from other tasks' `blockedBy` lists.
  - Tools: `task_create`, `task_update` (status/dependencies), `task_list`, `task_get`.
- **Notable insight:** "State that survives compression — because it's outside the conversation."

---

## `agents/s08_background_tasks.py` — Background Tasks
- **Purpose:** Non-blocking command execution via threads, with a notification queue drained before each LLM call.
- **Key components:**
  - `BackgroundManager` — `run()` spawns a daemon `threading.Thread`, returns short UUID immediately; `_execute()` captures output (300s timeout); `drain_notifications()` is thread-safe (lock-protected).
  - Notifications are injected into the next user turn as `<background-results>…</background-results>`.
  - Tools: `background_run`, `check_background`.
- **Notable dependencies:** `threading`, `uuid`.
- **Notable insight:** "Fire and forget — the agent doesn't block while the command runs."

---

## `agents/s09_agent_teams.py` — Agent Teams
- **Purpose:** Persistent named teammates, each running their own agent loop in a thread, communicating via file-based JSONL inboxes.
- **Key components:**
  - `MessageBus` — append-only `.team/inbox/<name>.jsonl` files; `read_inbox()` drains and clears.
  - `TeammateManager` — maintains `.team/config.json` with members (name, role, status: `idle`/`working`/`shutdown`); `_teammate_loop()` runs an agent loop with up to 50 iterations.
  - Defines 5 valid message types: `message`, `broadcast`, `shutdown_request`, `shutdown_response`, `plan_approval_response`.
  - Lead tools: `spawn_teammate`, `list_teammates`, `send_message`, `read_inbox`, `broadcast`.
  - REPL commands: `/team`, `/inbox`.
- **Contrast with s04:** Subagents are ephemeral; teammates are persistent and can be re-messaged.
- **Notable insight:** "Teammates that can talk to each other."

---

## `agents/s10_team_protocols.py` — Team Protocols
- **Purpose:** Structured handshakes between teammates using a `request_id` correlation pattern.
- **Key components:**
  - **Shutdown FSM:** `pending → approved | rejected`. Lead sends `shutdown_request{request_id}`; teammate replies `shutdown_response{request_id, approve, reason}`; thread exits if approved.
  - **Plan approval FSM:** `pending → approved | changes_requested`. Teammate submits `plan_approval{plan, request_id}`; lead reviews via `plan_approval{request_id, approve, feedback}`.
  - Module-level `shutdown_requests` / `plan_requests` dicts under `_tracker_lock`.
  - Handlers: `handle_shutdown_request`, `handle_plan_review`, `handle_plan_approval`.
- **Notable insight:** "Protocols give the team structure — not just chatter."

---

## `agents/s11_autonomous_agents.py` — Autonomous Agents
- **Purpose:** Teammates that can self-direct when idle — poll for work and claim unassigned tasks.
- **Key components:**
  - **WORK→IDLE→resume lifecycle:** After completing a task, a teammate signals `idle`; polls every 5s (max 60s) for inbox messages OR unclaimed tasks.
  - `scan_unclaimed_tasks()` / `claim_task()` — atomic claim via `.tasks/<id>.lock` files.
  - `make_identity_block()` — re-injects `<identity>` block after long pauses so a teammate remembers who it is.
- **Notable insight:** "Agents that can find their own work."

---

## `agents/s12_worktree_task_isolation.py` — Worktree + Task Isolation
- **Purpose:** Directory-level isolation for parallel execution using git worktrees.
- **Key components:**
  - `detect_repo_root()` — finds git root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
  - `EventBus` — lifecycle events stored in-memory + persisted to `.worktrees/events.jsonl`.
  - `TaskManager` — extended to track `worktree_id` per task.
  - `WorktreeManager` — manages worktrees in `.worktrees/<name>/`, tracks in `.worktrees/index.json`.
  - Tools: `worktree_create`, `worktree_remove`, `worktree_list`, `eventbus_list`.
- **Notable insight:** "Parallel execution without collisions."

---

## `agents/s_full.py` — Full Reference Agent
- **Purpose:** ~37 KB capstone combining all mechanisms from s01–s11.
- **Key components:** Integrates `TodoManager`, `SkillLoader`, `TaskManager`, `BackgroundManager`, `MessageBus`, `TeammateManager`, all protocol handlers, and micro/auto compact. REPL commands: `/compact`, `/tasks`, `/team`, `/inbox`.
- **Notable:** Not a teaching file — it's the integrated reference for everything.

---

## Summary Table

| File | Lesson |
|------|--------|
| `__init__.py` | Directory marker |
| `s01_agent_loop.py` | The fundamental agent loop |
| `s02_tool_use.py` | Tool dispatch map + file ops |
| `s03_todo_write.py` | Self-planning via TodoManager |
| `s04_subagent.py` | Context isolation via subagents |
| `s05_skill_loading.py` | Lazy-loaded skills |
| `s06_context_compact.py` | Memory compression (3 tiers) |
| `s07_task_system.py` | Persistent tasks w/ dependencies |
| `s08_background_tasks.py` | Background execution |
| `s09_agent_teams.py` | Named teammates w/ mailboxes |
| `s10_team_protocols.py` | Shutdown & plan approval protocols |
| `s11_autonomous_agents.py` | WORK→IDLE→resume lifecycle |
| `s12_worktree_task_isolation.py` | Git worktree isolation |
| `s_full.py` | Capstone reference |
